name: Schuyler Colfax
offices_summary: U.S. Representative, Indiana 9th district (1855-1869); Speaker of the U.S. House (1863-1869); Vice President of the United States (1869-1873)
summary: Moved with his family to South Bend in 1841 and edited the South Bend Free Press from 1842, buying it in 1845 and renaming it the St. Joseph Valley Register. He served in the U.S. House from 1855 to 1869, including as Speaker from 1863, and as Vice President from 1869 to 1873. He belonged to the Whig Party and later the Republican Party. His son Schuyler Colfax III served as mayor of South Bend.
documented_findings: A 1872-73 congressional investigation found that he accepted a $1,200 check for 20 shares of Credit Mobilier stock from Oakes Ames in 1868 (per Wikipedia); an impeachment resolution failed and he did not run for office again.
notes: Party code O = Whig (earlier affiliation); R = Republican.

name: Schuyler Colfax III
offices_summary: Mayor of South Bend (1898-1902; the Colfax article gives 1898-1901)
summary: Son of Vice President Schuyler Colfax. The Wikipedia mayors list shows him as the Republican mayor of South Bend from 1898 to 1902, while the article on his father gives 1898 to 1901.
notes: The 'youngest mayor' remark in the mayors list has no stated basis and is not encoded.

name: William G. George
offices_summary: Mayor of South Bend (1865-1868)
summary: Listed as the first mayor of South Bend after the city was incorporated on May 22, 1865. The Wikipedia mayors list gives his term as 1865 to 1868 and his party as Republican. No other biographical information was collected.

name: Janet Allen
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council (elected 1963); Republican nominee for mayor (1971)
summary: Wikipedia's page on South Bend mayoral elections identifies her as the first woman elected to the Common Council, in 1963. She was the Republican nominee for mayor in 1971 and lost to Jerry Miller.
notes: Single secondary source; no council dates collected.

name: Lloyd M. Allen
offices_summary: Mayor of South Bend (1964-1972)
summary: Elected mayor in 1963 and re-elected in 1967. He is identified as the last Republican elected mayor of South Bend; every mayor since 1972 has been a Democrat.
notes: Last Republican mayor confirmed against the Wikipedia table in the fact-check.

name: Jerry Miller
offices_summary: Mayor of South Bend (1972-1975; a sidebar gives 1972-85)
summary: Won the 1971 mayoral election, which began continuous Democratic control of the mayor's office. He campaigned on a cabinet form of government and restructured the executive branch after taking office. Sources differ on the end of his term (1975 in the table, 1985 in a sidebar).
notes: Wikipedia mayoral-elections page implies Miller served through December 1975 and Peter Nemeth from January 1976.

name: John Brademas
offices_summary: U.S. Representative, Indiana 3rd district (1959-1981); House Majority Whip (1977-1981); president of New York University (1981-1991 or 1992)
summary: Born in Mishawaka. He served 22 years in the U.S. House and lost his 1980 re-election bid to John Hiler.
notes: 'First Greek-American member of Congress' was not checked in the fact-check and is not encoded as FIRST. HIGHER applies (federal office); TENURE does not, because the U.S. House is not one of the governments the rule counts.

name: Tim Roemer
offices_summary: U.S. Representative, Indiana 3rd district (1991-2003); U.S. Ambassador to India (2009-2011)
summary: Born in South Bend. He defeated John Hiler in 1990 and served six terms in the U.S. House. He chaired the New Democrat Coalition from 1997 to 2001, served on the 9/11 Commission and was U.S. Ambassador to India from 2009 to 2011.
notes: HIGHER applied to anyone documented in a federal or statewide office (see _corrections file).

name: Joe Kernan
offices_summary: South Bend Controller (1980-1984); Mayor of South Bend (1988-1997); Lieutenant Governor of Indiana (1997-2003); Governor of Indiana (September 2003-January 2005)
summary: A Navy flight officer, he was shot down over North Vietnam and held as a prisoner of war for about 11 months. He became governor in September 2003 on the death of Gov. Frank O'Bannon and lost the 2004 governor's race to Mitch Daniels. His successor as mayor, Steve Luecke, was chosen by the South Bend Common Council in 1997.
notes: Governor and Lt. Governor dates match the standard record (fact-check, knowledge-only); cite an official state source before publication. Luecke's 1997 selection mechanism rests on one source.

name: Stephen Luecke
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council, 1st District (1988-1997); Mayor of South Bend (1997-2012)
summary: Joined the Common Council in 1988 and became mayor in January 1997 after Joe Kernan was elected lieutenant governor; he was then elected in 1999, 2003 and 2007. The Wikipedia mayors list shows his term as the longest of any mayor, 14 years and 363 days.
notes: TENURE counts council plus mayoral service in the same city (about 24 years). Wikipedia gives both 2011 and 2012 as the end year; the list says Jan 1, 2012.

name: Pete Buttigieg
offices_summary: Mayor of South Bend (2012-2020); U.S. Secretary of Transportation (2021-2025)
summary: Took office as mayor on January 1, 2012 at age 29 and was re-elected in 2015. He served as U.S. Secretary of Transportation from February 2021 to January 2025.
notes: Settlement figures corrected per fact-check ($75,000 + $500,000, not 'over $800,000'). Appeal status after June 2026 not confirmed (the fact-check report says the Council filed an appeal; WNDU 2026-06-02 says it was considering one).

name: Joe Donnelly
offices_summary: U.S. Representative, Indiana 2nd district (2007-2013); U.S. Senator (2013-2019); U.S. Ambassador to the Holy See (2022-2024)
summary: Served on the board of Marian High School, a private school in Mishawaka, from 1997 to 2001 before election to the U.S. House in 2006. He represented Indiana in the U.S. Senate from 2013 to 2019 and lost his 2018 re-election bid. He lives in Granger.
notes: Two Commons portraits exist (Representative; Ambassador).

name: Jackie Walorski
offices_summary: Indiana House, 21st district (2005-2010); U.S. Representative, Indiana 2nd district (2013-2022)
summary: Born in South Bend. She served in the Indiana House from January 2005 to November 2010 and in the U.S. House from January 2013 until her death on August 3, 2022 in a car crash near Nappanee. She was ranking member of the House Ethics Committee in 2021-22.

name: Rudy Yakym
offices_summary: U.S. Representative, Indiana 2nd district (since the 2022 special election)
summary: Won the special election held after the death of Rep. Jackie Walorski in August 2022.
notes: in_office_now reflects the term ending January 2027; the 2026 district-wide result was not checked, so succession in January 2027 is unknown.

name: B. Patrick Bauer
offices_summary: Indiana House, 6th district (1970-2020); Speaker of the Indiana House (two periods, dates differ across sources); House Minority Leader (2011)
summary: Served in the Indiana House from November 1970 to November 2020; Wikipedia describes him as the longest-serving member of the House and the first General Assembly member to serve 50 years. In February 2011 he led 37 Democrats in a walkout to block a right-to-work bill; it ended on March 28, 2011. His father, Burnie Bauer, served in the legislature, and his daughter, Maureen Bauer, succeeded him in the 6th district.
notes: Walkout count corrected to 37 (Ballotpedia via fact-check; Wikipedia said 36). Speaker years in Wikipedia (2003-05, 2007-11) are unverified; knowledge suggests 2002-04 and 2007-10. 'First to serve 50 years' rests on Wikipedia alone.

name: Burnie Bauer
offices_summary: State representative and state senator (dates and district not collected)
summary: Father of B. Patrick Bauer. Wikipedia's article on his son states that he served as a state representative and a state senator. Dates and districts were not collected.
notes: Party not documented. Included because the FAMILY criterion (two or more family members in elected office here) is met on the Bauer family.

name: Maureen Bauer
offices_summary: Indiana House, 6th district (since November 2020)
summary: Succeeded her father, B. Patrick Bauer, in the 6th district in November 2020; Wikipedia gives two start dates, November 4 and November 16, 2020.

name: Michael Dvorak
offices_summary: Indiana House, 8th district (1986-2002); St. Joseph County Prosecutor (2003-2015)
summary: Won the House seat in 1986 by defeating three-term Republican incumbent Lloyd Taylor and served until 2002. He was county prosecutor from January 2003 to January 2015 and did not seek re-election in 2014. His son Ryan Dvorak succeeded him in the House seat.
notes: A December 2010 charging decision in a case involving a private individual and a 2013 special-prosecutor request were omitted: the first per the fact-check's editorial instruction, the second because it is unverified.

name: Ryan Dvorak
offices_summary: Indiana House, 8th district (2002-present); Assistant Democratic Leader (after 2012)
summary: Succeeded his father, Michael Dvorak, in House District 8 in 2002. He ran in the 2011 Democratic primary for South Bend mayor and was a senior aide to Tim Roemer from 1996 to 2001.
notes: 2026 District 8 figures are unofficial (county document 73081, dated 11/3/2026).

name: Craig Fry
offices_summary: Indiana House, 5th district (1988-2012)
summary: Represented the Mishawaka area in the Indiana House for 24 years. Dale DeVon (R) won the open seat in 2012. Fry was an Ivy Tech apprenticeship director and the 2011 Democratic nominee for Mishawaka mayor, losing to Dave Wood.
notes: Sparse biography.

name: David Niezgodski
offices_summary: Indiana House, 7th district (2006-2016); Indiana Senate, 10th district (2016-present)
summary: Served in the Indiana House from November 2006 to November 2016 and in the Indiana Senate since November 2016. His spouse, Sheila Niezgodski, is a member of the South Bend Common Council. He won the 2024 Democratic primary over Tim Swager.
notes: Reported by WVPE (citing IndyStar), 2024-04-18: a former office assistant at his plumbing business filed an Indiana Civil Rights Commission complaint in 2017 and dropped it in exchange for $8,000. His statement expressed regret, took 'full responsibility' for any pain or discomfort, described the matter as a personnel issue resolved 'mutually and confidentially', and did not admit harassment. No charges or findings were reported. Not placed in documented_findings because it is not an official finding; details of the alleged conduct omitted per the fact-check.

name: Sheila Niezgodski
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council, 6th District (since 2019)
summary: Won the 2019 Democratic primary and general election for District 6; her second term began on January 1, 2024. She is the spouse of State Sen. David Niezgodski.

name: Ryan Mishler
offices_summary: Indiana Senate, 9th district (2004-present)
summary: Has held the 9th district Senate seat since 2004 and chairs the Appropriations Committee. He is a funeral director in Bremen. Wikipedia describes the district as spanning Kosciusko, Marshall, St. Joseph and Elkhart counties; he was unopposed in 2024.
notes: District boundaries after redistricting not re-checked.

name: Robert Beutter
offices_summary: Mayor of Mishawaka (1984-2003)
summary: Served five terms and was described by WSBT and the city as the longest-serving mayor in Mishawaka's history. He began as assistant city attorney under Mayor Margaret Prickett. He died in January 2020 at age 84.
notes: Party not stated in the WSBT or ABC57 obituaries. The Tribune's Kovach obituary (2022-11-21) says no Democrat has been elected mayor of Mishawaka since 1979, which excludes D but does not name his party.

name: Margaret Prickett
offices_summary: Mayor of Mishawaka (elected 1963; lost in 1979)
summary: Elected mayor of Mishawaka in 1963 and served four terms, about 16 years, until losing in 1979 to Democrat Bob Kovach. Robert Beutter began his career as assistant city attorney under her.
notes: Party R per the South Bend Tribune (2022-11-21). Dates still from search summaries (confidence stays low). 'First woman mayor' is unverified and not encoded.

name: Dave Wood
offices_summary: Mayor of Mishawaka (since 2010)
summary: Took over in 2010 to finish Jeff Rea's term and was elected in 2011, 2015, 2019 and 2023, unopposed in 2023. A city source describes him as Mishawaka's 21st mayor.
notes: TENURE is not fully documented: the month he took office in 2010 was not found, so 16 years of service is reached in late 2026 or 2027 depending on that date. '21st mayor' rests on a single WNDU source.

name: Karen White
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council, at-large (first elected 1999)
summary: First elected to the Common Council in 1999 according to Wikipedia, and re-elected to an at-large seat in November 2023.
notes: Continuous service from 1999 is assumed, not documented year by year.

name: Eugenia Braboy
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council, district seat (1984-1987)
summary: A 2003 city resolution names her as the first African American to hold a district seat on the South Bend Common Council and as the first African American woman on the council. The resolution page was seen only in search-result summaries and has not been read in full.
notes: Resolution seen only in a search summary; party not documented.

name: Pfeifer (given name unconfirmed: Beverly or Charlotte)
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council (1996-2007); council president (2000)
summary: According to a WVPE profile, she served on the council from 1996 to 2007 and was its first African American president, in 2000. Sources conflict on her first name.
notes: Use the city resolution's wording for the name before publication. Party not documented.

name: Sherry Bolden-Simpson
offices_summary: South Bend Common Council, 5th District (since January 1, 2024)
summary: Won District 5 in November 2023 over incumbent Eli Wax. The City of South Bend's council page states she is the first Democrat elected to the seat since 1962 and the first woman and first Black woman to hold it (not independently verified).
notes: Margin corrected to 38 per official canvass (fact-check). District 5 had elected Republicans since at least the early 1990s (WVPE).

name: J. Chester Allen
offices_summary: Indiana House of Representatives (elected 1938 and 1940)
summary: The Indiana Historical Bureau states that in 1938 voters elected him the first African American to represent St. Joseph County, and its state historical marker says he was elected state representative in 1938 and 1940 and introduced bills barring discrimination in employment and the judicial system. He and his wife, Elizabeth Fletcher Allen, ran a law firm in South Bend from 1939.
notes: The article's wording that he was 'the first person elected to serve on the South Bend Common Council' is removed per the fact-check (council dates from 1865). Remaining 'firsts' are single-snippet and need re-sourcing. Party and dates not documented.

name: John Hiler
offices_summary: U.S. Representative, Indiana 3rd district (1981-1991)
summary: Took office in January 1981 after defeating John Brademas in the 1980 election and served five terms; left office in January 1991 after losing to Tim Roemer in 1990.
